name: SonarCloud
description: Read-only SonarCloud code-quality access: projects in one organization, a project's quality measures (bugs, vulnerabilities, code smells, coverage) and its open issues. No issue transitions, assignment or project provisioning.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List the SonarCloud projects in one organization that this token can see (key, name, visibility, last analysis date, analysed revision)

q.description: Optional search string; matches project names and project keys that contain it

tools.name: project_measures
tools.description: Get the current quality measures for one SonarCloud component: bugs, vulnerabilities, code smells and coverage. A metric with no analysis is absent from the list rather than zero

component.description: Component key: a project key from list_projects, or a file key within it (e.g. my-org_my-project)

tools.name: list_issues
tools.description: Search SonarCloud issues in one organization, optionally narrowed to given components, impact severities or issue statuses (rule, severity, status, file, line, message, effort)

component_keys.description: Optional comma-separated component keys to scope the search to (a project key, or a file key within it)

impact_severities.description: Optional comma-separated impact severities: INFO, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, BLOCKER

issue_statuses.description: Optional comma-separated issue statuses: OPEN, CONFIRMED, FALSE_POSITIVE, ACCEPTED, FIXED

resolved.description: Optional: true returns only resolved issues, false only unresolved

needs_review: AUTH KEPT AS SCAFFOLDED AND CONFIRMED LIVE: basic with userField token and an empty passField matches integrationTypeRegistry.js key sonarcloud, whose testHeaders is ``'Authorization': `Basic ${Buffer.from(`${creds.token}:`).toString('base64')}```. Verified against the live host 2026-09-12: /api/authentication/validate answers 200 {"valid":false} to a dummy token (an unauthenticated session is a valid answer there, not an error), while every data path answers 401 with content-length: 0 and NO WWW-Authenticate header.

BASE_URL MOVED FROM https://sonarcloud.io TO https://sonarcloud.io/api, and the tool paths lost their /api prefix to match: the requests fired are byte-identical either way, the change is purely so the shape-proof control probe lands on the API surface instead of the marketing site. Evidence 2026-09-12: with the site-root base, the harness control path answers 200 text/html (the SonarCloud SPA catch-all), which is unusable as a differential and would push every empty-bodied 401 to AMBIGUOUS. Under /api the same control answers 401 with a zero-length body, exactly as the real paths do, so the run classifies as AUTH_WALL: SonarCloud rejects an invalid token BEFORE it routes. Anonymously (no Authorization header at all) that control path answers 404 {"errors":[{"msg":"Unknown url : /api/quox-shapeproof-control-<hash>"}]}, which shows routing exists but is unreachable behind the wall. The PATHS therefore rest on the published web-api registry below, not on this run.

PATHS, PARAMS AND CLAMPS COME FROM THE LIVE SELF-DESCRIBING REGISTRY https://sonarcloud.io/api/webservices/list (fetched 2026-09-12, anonymous, 200). Verbatim: api/projects search is 'Search for projects. Results are filtered to projects the caller has access to.' with organization required=true, 'The key of the organization', and ps 'Page size. Must be greater than 0 and less or equal than 500' defaultValue 100 maximumValue 500. api/measures component is 'Return component with specified measures. The componentId or the component parameter must be provided.
Requires the following permission: 'Browse' on the project of specified component.' with metricKeys required=true, 'Comma-separated list of metric keys'. api/issues search is 'Search for issues.
Requires the 'Browse' permission on the specified project(s).' with ps defaultValue 50 maximumValue 500. The ps cap was also checked live on a public organization: ps=500 returns 200, ps=501 returns 400 {"errors":[{"msg":"'ps' value (501) must be less than 500"}]}. Hence clamp 100 500 and clamp 50 500.

THE METRIC SET IS A FIXED LITERAL, NOT AN ARGUMENT: metricKeys is required=true and spec v1.1 has no default-value helper (clamp is the only helper, and it is numeric), so an unsupplied optional input would render empty, be dropped from the query and 400 the call. project_measures therefore hard-codes bugs,vulnerabilities,code_smells,coverage. Widening the metric set means editing this spec or adding a defaulting helper to spec v1.1; it is not something a caller can pass. The four keys were checked live and anonymously against a public project on 2026-09-12 and all four came back: {"component":{..."measures":[{"metric":"coverage","value":"89.2","bestValue":false},{"metric":"bugs","value":"40","bestValue":false},{"metric":"code_smells","value":"866","bestValue":false},{"metric":"vulnerabilities","value":"0","bestValue":true}]}}. A metric the project has never analysed is ABSENT from that array rather than zero, which is why the tool description says so: a missing coverage entry must never be read as 0% coverage.

NON-DEPRECATED FILTERS CHOSEN DELIBERATELY: the same registry marks the old issue filters deprecated, severities deprecatedSince '25 Aug, 2023', types '25 Aug, 2023', statuses '03 Jul, 2024', resolutions '03 Jul, 2024'. list_issues therefore exposes impactSeverities (possibleValues INFO, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, BLOCKER) and issueStatuses (possibleValues OPEN, CONFIRMED, FALSE_POSITIVE, ACCEPTED, FIXED). Both are comma-separated LISTS in the API, so they are declared as plain strings with the accepted values spelled out in the input description rather than as single-value enums, which would have blocked the multi-value form the API documents.

ORGANIZATION IS REQUIRED ON list_issues THOUGH THE API DOES NOT REQUIRE IT: in the registry the issues/search organization param is required=false, but an unscoped search is a global one. Checked live and anonymously 2026-09-12: /api/issues/search?ps=2 with no scope answers 400, and the same call with organization=apache answers 200 with issues. Requiring the key here means the tool can neither 400 for lack of scope nor return cross-organization noise. The API-level truth (optional) is recorded here so nobody later reads this spec as documentation of the endpoint.

RESPONSE PICKS COME FROM THE DOCUMENTED RESPONSE EXAMPLES at https://sonarcloud.io/api/webservices/response_example (controller=api/projects action=search, controller=api/measures action=component, controller=api/issues action=search), fetched 2026-09-12. Two honest gaps: the live issues payload also carries top-level total/p/ps beside paging, and the picks read paging.* because that is the shape the documented example declares; and an issue today carries BOTH the old model's 'severity' (INFO/MINOR/MAJOR/CRITICAL/BLOCKER) and the new model's 'issueStatus', so both are picked rather than guessing which model an organization is on.

PROBE VALUES ARE PUBLIC DATA: _probe supplies organization 'apache' and component/componentKeys 'apache_juneau', a public SonarCloud organization and project (both verified anonymously 2026-09-12, 200 with real data), plus impactSeverities 'HIGH', issueStatuses 'OPEN' and q 'juneau' because the harness's generic dummy 'quoxprobe' is not a valid value for the first two. All are world-readable and read-only, credentials are never hinted, and _probe sits at TOOL level where the harness reads it (a _probe nested inside request is silently ignored).

READ-ONLY BY CHOICE: SonarCloud also exposes write surfaces (issue transitions and assignment via api/issues/do_transition and api/issues/assign, project provisioning via api/projects/create). None are exposed here. Changing an issue's state is a governance-relevant act on someone's quality gate, so it stays out of this connector rather than shipping half-guarded.
